title: TS SDK: checkpointed stream bridge for async-iterator <-> Web Streams interoperability
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: TS SDK users need ergonomic helpers that let application code seamlessly convert between async iterators (for server-driven streaming idioms) and browser/node ReadableStreams without leaking memory or losing the ability to resume partially-read streams. We also need patterns for checkpointing/resuming long-running streaming responses (for poor network conditions or process restarts).

Goal: Implement a "checkpointed" stream bridge helper in the TypeScript SDK that: 1) converts AsyncIterable<Chunk> -> ReadableStream, 2) converts ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable, 3) exposes a lightweight checkpoint token API for saving/resuming stream position (KV-cache key or opaque resume token), and 4) maps cancellation/backpressure cleanly across runtimes (Node/Deno/Browser).

Scope: Add new helper module `streaming/bridge.ts` with exported functions: `asyncIterableToReadableStreamWithCheckpoint`, `readableStreamToAsyncIterableWithResume`. Provide examples in SDK docs and three integration tests (node, deno, browser). Instrument with tracing hooks and metrics so Console can show resumed stream counts.

Non-goals: Not changing existing public generation API shapes, not introducing protocol changes to the hosted API (resume will be best-effort and use existing model `cursor` metadata where available). Full server-side resume orchestration (to be a separate infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Helper functions compile with no breaking changes in existing SDK surface
Bridge correctly converts AsyncIterable->ReadableStream and back in Node, Deno, and Chromium-based browsers
Checkpoint token can be generated and consumed to resume a stream from the same logical position (best-effort across model variants)
Cancellation from either side closes the underlying connection and releases resources (no memory leak after repeated create/destroy)
Automated tests cover simulated intermittent network (resume from last checkpoint) and backpressure scenarios
Documentation snippet and a runnable example included in the repository examples/streaming/bridge/
design_decisions: Expose checkpoint token as opaque string to avoid coupling SDK to server internals
Prefer pull-based resume points (byte/count-based) when server returns stable offsets, fallback to last-successful-chunk token when offsets unavailable
Do not change top-level streaming API signatures; provide helpers in a new opt-in module to avoid surprising existing users
Map ReadableStream backpressure to AsyncIterator by pausing the underlying source and buffering up to a configurable window (default 4 items)
On cancellation, propagate AbortSignal to all internal helpers and emit a single 'cleanup' trace point for Console observability
implementation_notes: Create sources/ts/sdk/streaming/bridge.ts with strongly typed generics and JSDoc examples
Add runtime adapters: node (stream.Readable.from), deno (ReadableStream polyfill), browser (native ReadableStream)
Implement a tiny in-memory checkpoint manager interface with pluggable persistence (default: no-op; tests use local variable; later ticket will add Dedicated KV integration)
Add unit tests under tests/streaming/bridge.spec.ts and integration/bridge-browser.test.ts (playwright)
Perf budget: bridge overhead < 5% token throughput and < 3ms median per-chunk latency on microbenchmarks
Add Console metric: sdk.stream.resume.count and sdk.stream.resume.latency
Docs: examples/streaming/bridge/README.md with copy-and-paste examples for Node/Deno/Browser
Backwards compat check: run repo-wide TypeScript build and run ts-sdk integration smoke tests
comments: 2025-02-18 - Triage: Accepted by eng lead (Maya Patel). Assigned to Diego for spike. Priority set to P1 due to customer requests for resumable streaming.

2025-02-22 - Spike: prototype shows AsyncIterable->ReadableStream conversion feasible with small wrapper. Observed backpressure mismatch in Chrome: when consumer is slow, underlying generator kept producing until internal buffer limit. Added configurable buffer window in prototype.

2025-02-26 - Design review: Reviewed with PM (Samir Kaur) and DX (Jules Moretti). Decided to keep checkpoint token opaque and opt-in; avoid server-side API changes in this ticket. PM requested a clear UX example for failure scenarios.

2025-02-28 - Engineering: Opened draft PR with initial adapter implementations and unit tests. Added instrumentation hooks for resume count. Benchmarks: prototype overhead ~2.1% throughput, median additional latency 1.6ms per chunk (node v20).

2025-03-03 - Review feedback from reviewer (Maya Patel): please add browser-playwright test and ensure AbortSignal propagation across Deno's polyfill. Diego will address and update PR. Also add a short migration note for users relying on raw ReadableStream behavior.
Next steps: finish browser tests, add example snippet to docs, run leak/regression test harness, and promote PR out of draft. Plan to demo to PM and Docs on 2025-03-10.
notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the server resume contract best-effort. If we discover incompatible model variants, fallback will be explicit and surfaced in Console as 'resume_failed' event.
